title: Drop a yo-yo beside a ball. Which lands first? The ball at 0.45 s; the yo-yo 1.97 s, 4.36x later
description:
Drop a yo-yo beside a ball. Which lands first? One scene, side view, both on one height scale. The yo-yo is a uniform solid disc of radius R = 3 cm (6 cm across; its mass m cancels, and the axle's own mass counts as part of the disc) on an axle of radius r = 0.5 cm (1 cm across), R / r = 6, I = m R^2 / 2. Its 1 m string is wound on the axle and tied to it, a hand holds the top end still, and the yo-yo is let go from rest with the string taut and vertical; the string does not slip or stretch, so x = r phi. Beside it a ball of the same size (radius 3 cm) is dropped from the same height at the same instant and falls freely at g = 9.807 m/s^2 with no air drag; the floor stops it, no bounce. Both centres drop exactly 1.00 m: the ball lands, and the yo-yo reaches the end of its string with its rim level with the floor. There the string, tied to the axle, reverses the yo-yo's downward speed while the spin keeps its sense and the string winds on again on the other side: an ideal turnaround with no loss (a real yo-yo loses some each turn). The equations m x'' = m g - T and I phi'' = T r with x = r phi give a = g / (1 + (R / r)^2 / 2) = g / 19 = 0.5162 m/s^2 and T = 18 / 19 of the weight, for any mass and any string length. Integrated by classical RK4 at 10000 steps per second (dt = 1e-04 s) with the tension from the constraint each step and compensated summation, the end of the string and the stop at the top located by bisection inside the step, a half-step rerun as a check, against the closed forms. Shown at 1/2 speed on a 10 s cycle, 4 drops in 40 s. Deterministic, no seed.

Measured:
- the ball: lands at sqrt(2 h / g) = 0.4516 s (under half a second) at 4.43 m/s; stepped at the same dt 0.451593 s (diff +2.2e-14 s)
- the yo-yo: reaches the end of its string at 1.9684 s (closed form sqrt(2 h / a), diff -8.9e-16 s), 1.517 s after the ball, 4.3589 times later (exactly sqrt(19), diff -2.7e-15), moving at 1.016 m/s and spinning at 203.21 rad/s = 1,940 turns a minute (32.3 turns a second), 31.83 turns in all; 19685 RK4 steps down
- when the ball lands at 0.4516 s the yo-yo has dropped 5.26 cm (closed form a t^2 / 2 = 5.26 cm) at 0.233 m/s and 445 turns a minute, against the ball's 4.43 m/s
- the string holds T / (m g) = 0.947368 of the weight = 94.74 percent (18 / 19, diff +0.0e+00), constant down and up
- energy at the bottom per unit mass: g h = 9.8070 J/kg = 0.5162 J/kg in the fall (5.26 percent, 1 / 19) plus 9.2908 J/kg in the spin (94.74 percent, 18 / 19); the balance holds within 1.4e-14 J/kg over the drop and the climb; the no-slip residual x - r phi stays within 1.0e-15 m down and 1.6e-15 m up
- the turnaround at 1.9684 s: 1.0160 m/s down becomes 1.0160 m/s up, the spin stays 203.21 rad/s; the yo-yo stops rising at 3.9369 s (closed form 2 sqrt(2 h / a), diff -1.3e-15 s; 8.72 times the ball's fall) at -2.4e-16 m from the hand with speed 0.0e+00 m/s: back in the hand at rest; 19685 steps up
- half-step rerun (dt = 5e-05 s): the end of the string at 1.9684469 s, the top at 3.9368939 s, the speed at the bottom 1.0160294 m/s, each +0.0e+00 against the full step
- the drop (real time since the release): 0.25 s: yo-yo 1.6 cm down, 0.129 m/s, 246 rpm, ball 30.6 cm, 2.45 m/s; 0.50 s: yo-yo 6.5 cm, 0.258 m/s, 493 rpm, ball on the floor; 1.00 s: 25.8 cm, 0.516 m/s, 986 rpm; 1.50 s: 58.1 cm, 0.774 m/s, 1479 rpm; the climb mirrors it: 2.00 s: 96.8 cm down, 1.000 m/s up, 1909 rpm; 3.00 s: 22.7 cm, 0.484 m/s up, 924 rpm; 4.00 s: in the hand
- a 0.5 cm axle (R / r = 12): a = g / 73 = 0.1343 m/s^2, 3.858 s, 8.54 times the ball, the string holding 98.6 percent of the weight, 0.518 m/s and 207.3 rad/s = 1,980 rpm at the bottom
- a 2 cm axle (R / r = 3): a = g / 5.5 = 1.7831 m/s^2, 1.059 s, 2.35 times the ball, the string holding 81.8 percent, 1.888 m/s and 1,803 rpm
- a hollow ring yo-yo of the same size on the 1 cm axle (I = m R^2): a = g / 37 = 0.2651 m/s^2, 2.747 s, 6.08 times the ball, the string holding 97.3 percent, 0.728 m/s and 1,391 rpm

Why: the string is wound on the thin axle, so the yo-yo turns once for every 2 pi r of string, 31.83 turns in the metre, and the disc's inertia about its axle is 18 times m r^2. So 18 / 19 of the energy released by the fall goes into the spin and only 1 / 19 into moving down: the string holds back 94.74 percent of the weight and the yo-yo falls at g / 19, while the ball takes the whole g. The time ratio is sqrt(19) = 4.3589 for any height, mass or string length; only R / r matters, so a thinner axle (8.54 times) or a hollow rim (6.08 times) slows it more and a thicker axle (2.35 times) less. At the bottom the string winds on the other side with the spin unchanged, the same tension slows the climb, and the yo-yo is back in the hand at rest after exactly twice the drop time, 3.9369 s.

Rerun sims/yoyo/yoyo.py with projects/yoyo/manifest.json and you get these numbers exactly.
